name: Landscape Installation & Construction
summary: Planting, sod, patios, paths and low walls, built to a written plan and plant list.

seo.title: Landscape installation in Greater Victoria | RNC Landscaping
seo.description: Planting, sod, patios, paths and retaining walls in Greater Victoria, planned around your soil, slope and the tree bylaw for your lot. Ask for a free quote.

hero.h1: Landscape installation and construction in Greater Victoria
hero.lede: Planting, sod, patios, paths and low retaining walls, planned around clay or rocky soil, slope, deer and the tree bylaw that applies to your lot.

audiences.title: Homeowners
audiences.body: A front garden, backyard patio or new planting plan built in clear phases, with a written scope before any digging starts.

audiences.title: Stratas and property managers
audiences.body: Courtyard renewals, entrance plantings and replacements for failed shrubs, scheduled to limit disruption for residents.

audiences.title: General contractors and developers
audiences.body: Soft and hard landscape packages built to your drawings and schedule, with coordination through your site supervisor. See [commercial work](/commercial/).

includes.title: Design and layout
includes.body: A plan that fits the site: sun, drainage, slope, deer pressure and how you want to use the space.

includes.title: Planting
includes.body: Trees, shrubs and perennials suited to our dry summers and wet winters, including native and drought-tolerant choices.

includes.title: Sod and seed
includes.body: Soil preparation, grading, and new lawn installed with a watering plan that follows CRD new-sod rules.

includes.title: Hardscape
includes.body: Patios, paths, steps, edging and low retaining walls in stone or pavers.

includes.title: Drainage and soil
includes.body: Grading, soil amendment and simple drainage fixes so new planting is not sitting in winter water.

includes.title: Irrigation built in
includes.body: Drip or spray zones added during the build through our [irrigation service](/services/irrigation/).

goodFitIf.heading: Good fit if…
items: You want to replace lawn with planting that copes with dry summers and deer
Your yard holds water in winter or slopes toward the house
You have a designer's plan or contractor's drawings that need building
Your strata wants written options council can choose between
There is a protected tree near the work and you want the rules checked first
Planting before the summer dry spell
Planting trees and shrubs while the soil is warm and rain returns

process.title: Request a quote
process.body: Tell us what you have in mind on the [quote form](/free-quote/). Photos help.
process.deliverable: Your request, sent from your own email app

process.title: Site visit
process.body: We measure, check soil, slope and access, and look for protected trees or root zones near the work.
process.deliverable: Notes on the site and any rules that may apply

process.title: Plan and written scope
process.body: You get a layout, plant list and written scope, with any permits that may apply named up front.
process.deliverable: A layout, plant list and written scope

process.title: Build
process.body: We prepare the ground, install hardscape, then plant and mulch. You get an update as each phase finishes.

process.title: Walkthrough and care notes
process.body: We walk the finished work with you and leave watering and care notes for the first season.
process.deliverable: Written care notes for the first season

localRules.heading: Local rules that affect a build
localRules.intro: Most installation work needs no permit, but these rules come up often. We check them for your address before work starts.

items.text: Victoria's Tree Protection Bylaw: a permit may be needed to prune, remove or work in the root zone of a protected tree.
Esquimalt requires a tree permit to remove or prune a protected tree, or to work in its protected root zone, unless exempted.
CRD watering rules: new sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.
In Metchosin, where a stream or wetland is on or next to the property, the BC Riparian Areas Regulation may also apply.

localRules.areasLink: Every municipality has its own tree bylaw. Find yours on our [service area pages](/areas/).

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for my landscape project?
faqs.a: Many projects do not, but work near protected trees, on steep slopes or near watercourses may. We check the rules for your municipality and tell you what applies before we start. Read our [tree permit notes](/resources/winter-pruning-and-storm-prep/).

faqs.q: When is a good time to plant?
faqs.a: Fall often suits southern Vancouver Island because the rain returns and roots grow through the mild winter. Spring works too, with careful watering through the first summer.

faqs.q: Can you work from my designer's plan?
faqs.a: Yes. We can build from your plan or a general contractor's drawings.

faqs.q: How do quotes work for a project?
faqs.a: We quote each project from a site visit and a written scope. There is no charge for the quote, and the scope lists what is and is not included.

faqs.q: Can new sod be watered outside the lawn days?
faqs.a: The CRD says new sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary watering schedule. Check the current details on the [CRD watering page](https://www.crd.ca/environment/water-conservation/watering-schedule) or our [watering guide](/resources/crd-watering-rules-guide/).

faqs.q: What plants cope with deer and dry summers?
faqs.a: Many natives and Mediterranean shrubs do, such as Oregon grape, sword fern, salal, lavender and rosemary. Your plant list is chosen for the site. See our [native planting guide](/resources/native-and-drought-tolerant-planting/).
